---
title: "Reproducibility guarantees"
description: >
  What a key promises across platforms, threads, engines and package
  versions, and how that is kept.
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(zurand)
```

A zurand key always gives the same values. This article says exactly what
"always" covers: which changes leave the values alone, which change them,
and what the package does to keep that promise. It is for readers who
store keys with results, or who need to know that a result computed today
can be recomputed elsewhere later.

## What never changes the values

Draw `i` of a key depends only on the key, `i`, the sampler and its
arguments. In particular it does not depend on:

* **how many values are drawn**, so `rng_normal(key, 10)[1:3]` is
  `rng_normal(key, 3)`, and `offset` can start anywhere in the stream;
* **the order of calls**, or on anything else drawn in the session;
* **the platform**: Linux (glibc and musl), macOS and Windows, on x86_64
  and aarch64;
* **the number of threads** set with `rng_threads()`, or whether the SIMD
  path of `rng_simd()` is in use.

The thread count, for one, can be checked directly:

```{r}
key <- rng_key(2026)
old <- rng_threads(1)
one_thread <- rng_normal(key, 1e5)
rng_threads(old)
identical(one_thread, rng_normal(key, 1e5))
```

32-bit x86 builds, whose x87 floating point rounds differently, are outside
this guarantee.

## How that is kept

Uniform and integer draws use integer operations and single floating-point
operations, each correctly rounded, which IEEE 754 defines the same way on
every platform. That holds only if the compiler does not fuse a multiply
and an add into one instruction, which some do by default on ARM and which
changes a result by a rounding step, so zurand keeps every compiler from
doing it. Normal draws need one more step, because the ziggurat method's
rare slow path calls `exp()` and `log1p()`, and platforms' maths libraries
round those differently. zurand computes both with its own port of
fdlibm.

None of this is assumed. Every CI platform checks known answers for the
generators against independent reference implementations, pinned values
for every sampler, and hashes of whole streams of millions of draws, which
reach the slow path many times.

## Engines

A key records its **engine**, the generator behind its stream:

```{r}
attr(key, "engine")
attr(rng_key(2026, engine = "philox4x64"), "engine")
```

The default, `"xoshiro256pp"`, is the fastest. `"philox4x64"` and
`"threefry4x64"` are counter-based: each value is computed directly from
its position, which makes reading scattered positions of a lazy vector
faster. `?rng_key` describes each one.

All three give every guarantee above, but each gives different values. A
key made with one engine keeps it, so a saved key is safe; a key made from
a seed in code, `rng_key(2026)`, follows the package default. Name the
engine when a stream has to outlive a change of default:

```{r}
key <- rng_key(2026, engine = "xoshiro256pp")
```

## Stream versions

A key also records the version of the stream definition it was made
under:

```{r}
attr(key, "stream")
```

The values of every engine and stream version are frozen. If a defect in a
stream were ever found, the fix would become a new stream version for new
keys, and existing keys, saved ones included, would keep producing exactly
what they always have. A key from a newer stream than the installed zurand
knows is an error, never a silent reinterpretation.

New features keep the old values too: a new sampler method, such as
`rng_normal(method = "mcfarland")`, is a separate stream, and the default
method never changes.

## Folding is typed

`rng_fold()` derives a key from the type of its data as well as its value,
so a number and the string that prints the same way give different keys,
while an integer and a double holding the same whole number agree:

```{r}
identical(rng_fold(key, 1), rng_fold(key, 1L))
identical(rng_fold(key, 1), rng_fold(key, "1"))
```

Strings fold as their UTF-8 text, so the same name gives the same key in
any locale. Factors and dates are an error rather than folding as their
internal codes; `?rng_fold` has the details.

## Keys from R's generator

`rng_key_from_r()` is the one function that reads R's own generator. It
turns the current `set.seed()` state into a key, so a script that already
sets a seed can hand zurand a key derived from it:

```{r}
set.seed(1)
rng_key_from_r()
```

The key is then independent of R's generator: nothing drawn from it moves
`.Random.seed`.

guarantees to work.
